name: Serve first-strike change
definition: Per earlier covered match: k = own serve points won within 4 shots (ace, unreturned serve, serve-plus-one winner or forced error), n = own serve points with a real rally length, double faults excluded; e = logit((k+0.5)/(n+1)) minus the norms. Variant: points ended within 4 shots, whoever won
as_of_and_memory: Own matches with lf+1 <= es of the match; n-weighted mean of e over the last 28 days minus over days 29-364; no covered match in 28 days gives 0 and a missing flag
opponent_and_venue_adjustment: Surface norm + the returner's 52-week norm (how often servers win quickly against him) + the venue norm (earlier editions and earlier days, match clock, probe)
shrinkage: 28-day mean shrunk toward the longer mean by N28/(N28+K); K = sampling over between-match variance of e within players, from 2018-2024 spreads, no results
declared_direction: Positive: a recent rise in first-strike serving against his own norm means A beats the close
mechanism: Process measure of how the serve and first ball work right now, from every serve point; fatigue cut serve accuracy while speed held (Gescheit 2015) and second-serve win rate (Gescheit 2017); the same kind of state as the serve-speed change, which replicated given the model and the close
why_not_closed: Rally measures were only ever built as long-run levels; the only change feature was spd1_change (point-shot ideas item 1)
coverage_realistic: Tour-level matches where both players had a covered match in 28 days and a 52-week norm: mostly the 1000s (real rally lengths on 99% of main draws, 93% of qualifying), covered 250s/500s (44-49%), Wimbledon and the US Open; Challengers almost none (6-7%)
testable_at_tour_level: Computable on roughly 1,500-2,000 matches in 2025-26 (inferred); a speed-change-sized effect would read about z 1.8; not resolvable at plausible sizes
how_it_could_be_wrong: Noisy copy of the speed stage or the two-week box-score forms; venue confounds; surface switches inside 28 days; event-specific tracking counts

name: Return-neutralisation change
definition: Per earlier covered match: k = returns put in play (rally length 3 or more, or a return winner), n = opponent's serve points with a real rally length, double faults excluded; logit residual against the norms
as_of_and_memory: As R1: 28 days minus days 29-364, own matches with lf+1 <= es
opponent_and_venue_adjustment: Surface norm + the server's 52-week unreturned-serve norm + the venue norm (match clock, probe)
declared_direction: Positive: a recent rise in returns put in play against his own norm means A beats the close
mechanism: Returning is reaction, first step and footwork; sprint and jump fell on days 2-4 of back-to-back play, stretched returns rose; the box score holds return outcomes, not whether the return came back; the 2025-26 close under-rated returning (seen data)
why_not_closed: Returns in play was built only as a trait (split-half 0.86-0.91); never as a change
how_it_could_be_wrong: Big servers drive the variation, so the server norm carries the weight; not independent of the seen returning-under-rated finding; may proxy the model's return forms

name: Long-rally luck
definition: Per earlier covered match: N = points of 9+ shots, W = those won; E = N x expit(lambda_own - lambda_opp), lambda = career long-rally strength as of that match; D = W - E
as_of_and_memory: L = sum of 2^(-age/28 days) x D over matches in the 16 weeks before es, own matches with lf+1 <= es
opponent_and_venue_adjustment: lambda opponent-adjusted in one IOS-style pass (match clock, probe)
shrinkage: lambda shrunk with K about 152 long-rally points (shot-level Stage 1, men)
declared_direction: Negative: recent long-rally luck means A loses to the close (over-rated)
mechanism: Per point a long rally carries far less player signal than a quick point (Stage 1 K 152 against 41-44), so results built on long-rally wins are disproportionately luck; prices follow results; the luck family leans this way in every era and held in 2025-26; long rallies leave a one-point after-effect only
why_not_closed: Long-rally points won was tested only as a level (a trait, the opposite sign), -0.04 given the odds; the luck form never built
coverage_realistic: As R1 but a 16-week window, somewhat wider; tour level only
how_it_could_be_wrong: Long-rally wins may reflect a persisting physical state (sign flips); the model's two-week points-won forms absorb part; lambda is noisy; small effect on results (about 16 long rallies per 1000s match)

name: Within-event long-rally load
definition: LR = sum of exp(-gap/2 days) x N9 over own singles matches whose latest finish is at most 4 days before es; N9 = the match's points of 9+ shots; missing unless every match in the window has real rally lengths (never imputed); X = log(1+LR) - f(log(1+MIN), log(1+PTS)). Variants: total shots; X x [rest under 30 h]; X x the expected long-rally demand of the match
as_of_and_memory: 4-day window, decay constant 2 days, match clock gaps (lf to es)
opponent_and_venue_adjustment: None for load; f is a least-squares fit of the long-rally kernel on the minutes and points kernels over 2018-2024 player-matches with fully covered windows (outcome-free)
shrinkage: None (a count); the beyond-minutes residual is the feature
declared_direction: Negative: more long-rally load beyond minutes means A loses to the close
mechanism: Lactate rises with strokes per rally (r 0.43) and rally duration (0.51); back-to-back long days cut sprint and jump, raise muscle damage and errors; the market sees sets, scoreline and duration, not rally composition
why_not_closed: E4 intensity-weighted load was parked (47/100) and never built; minutes, sets and fatigue kernels were tested, shots and long rallies never
coverage_realistic: Later rounds with covered previous rounds: 97% of such player-rows at the 1000s, 46% at the 250s, 43% at the 500s, 4% at Challengers; first rounds have none unless a previous event ended within 4 days
testable_at_tour_level: Computable on about 1,000 matches in 2025-26 (inferred); too few for plausible effects
how_it_could_be_wrong: Minutes absorb most of it; survival bias; long rallies mark close matches the market sees; market over-reaction would flip the sign; heat and slow conditions; missingness follows show courts; no causal link to outcomes shown (Reid and Duffield 2014)

name: Venue rally pace as a price-slope modulator
encoding: Price-slope modulator: logit q = a + b logit p + c V logit p (variant: -V x (FS_A - FS_B), FS = 52-week share of own serve points won within 4 shots)
definition: V = the venue's shrunk mean of (rally length minus its expectation from the server's and returner's 52-week rally-length norms) over earlier editions (weight halved per year) and earlier days of this edition
as_of_and_memory: Earlier editions and earlier days only, match clock and probe
opponent_and_venue_adjustment: The players' norms remove who played there
shrinkage: Toward the surface norm with K from the spread between editions
declared_direction: c > 0: where rallies run longer than the players imply, the favourite beats the close; where shorter, the underdog
mechanism: Prices adjust for the surface but learn a venue's own pace slowly (pattern 3's mechanism); slower conditions mean fewer serve-decided points and tie-breaks, so skill shows more; rally length measures pace on every shot, not only through aces
why_not_closed: Venue pace exists only from aces (U-192, pattern 3); a rally-length pace was never built; whether pace x price was tried in the f10 price-slope family is unknown
coverage_realistic: Widest: needs venue history, not player depth: every 1000s match, the fully covered 250s and 500s, Wimbledon and the US Open, with earlier editions from the ATP handoff and P9
testable_at_tour_level: The most testable of the eight; needs pattern 3's term as a control
how_it_could_be_wrong: May re-find pattern 3 (in production, checked on 2025-26); the price's favourite-longshot curve must be fitted first; noisy early-edition norms

name: Rally-mix style clash
definition: Band edges on serve sigma(b) and return rho(b), b in {4 or fewer, 5-8, 9+}, and band-mix tendencies pi_s(b), pi_r(b); mix on A's serve pi_AB(b) proportional to pi_s_A(b) pi_r_B(b) / pi_bar(b) x the venue term; Delta_A = sum over b of [pi_AB(b) - pi_s_A(b)] x expit(mu_b + sigma_A(b) - rho_B(b)); Delta_B likewise
as_of_and_memory: 52-week memory, own and opponents' matches before es (match clock, probe)
opponent_and_venue_adjustment: Edges opponent-adjusted (IOS-style); mixes from point lengths only; venue term as R5
shrinkage: Each band edge shrunk with K from its spread (Stage 1: 9+ about 152)
declared_direction: Positive: when the mix this matchup produces favours A's band strengths, A beats the close
mechanism: Ratings and prices carry one serve and one return strength per player and surface; a grinder who drags a first-strike server into long rallies changes the point mix itself
why_not_closed: Finer matchups listed as not tested (shot-level Stage 3); boosting on 102 inputs a side found nothing with wide intervals
coverage_realistic: Tour-level matches where both players have 52-week band profiles (mostly 1000s regulars); Challengers almost none
testable_at_tour_level: Computable; very low power (9+ edges pass little of the truth)
how_it_could_be_wrong: The returner's elasticity against big servers, the closest test, was priced; noisy band edges; overlaps pattern 3 and the IOS profiles

name: Rally balance at depth
definition: B = opponent-adjusted logit edge in points of 5+ shots (serve and return pooled) minus the edge in points of 4 or fewer shots; only for players with at least 1,000 real-rally points in 52 weeks
as_of_and_memory: 52 weeks before es, own matches with lf+1 <= es
shrinkage: Each part shrunk with Stage 1's K (5+: 158; quick: 41-44, men)
declared_direction: Positive: relatively stronger in rallies than in first-strike points means A beats the close
mechanism: The 2025-26 close gave serving too much weight relative to returning at equal strength (serve_return_leads, seen data); first-strike points are where serving shows
why_not_closed: The separate noisy traits were data-limited (edges up to 1-2 mLL could hide); the balance form never built
coverage_realistic: The deepest players only (inferred top 60-100 men, 1000s); Challengers none
testable_at_tour_level: Computable on few matches; its 2025-26 reading is not independent of the serve-over-returning lead found in that window
how_it_could_be_wrong: Proxy of that lead; style traits have never beaten the close here; noisy 5+ edges

name: Net-approach change
definition: a = net approaches per point played (serve and return), flagged events only; 28-day mean minus 52-week mean
declared_direction: Negative (low confidence): coming forward more than usual read as shortening points to cope with fatigue
mechanism: Fatigued players moved less (Gescheit 2015); players adapt tactics to declining function (Reid and Duffield 2014)
why_not_closed: Net approaches and net points won were closed as traits; a change never built
coverage_realistic: 24 events; a median of 3 flagged matches per player in 22 months (observed)
how_it_could_be_wrong: Grass and conditions drive net play; the direction could equally be confidence
